title: Local Josephson response near nonmagnetic impurities and vortices in a two-orbital $s_{\pm}$ superconductor
abstract: We study the local Josephson response near nonmagnetic impurities and vortices in a self-consistent two-orbital $s_{\pm}$ superconductor. For a local $s$-wave tip that couples equally to the two orbitals, anomalous spectral contributions of opposite sign nearly cancel in the clean sample. Nonmagnetic impurities redistribute these contributions and can reverse the local coupling without a corresponding $π$ phase shift of the bond pair fields. Negative coupling appears at off-center sites at weaker impurity potentials than at the impurity site. The impurity-induced change is concentrated at lower quasiparticle energies, while states over a broader energy range contribute to the total clean and impurity couplings. In zero field, the coupling also changes sign as the tip gap is varied, and increasing the tunneling strength can reverse the $m=1$ sine component of the current without changing the sample state. At the chosen coherence-peak energy, increasing impurity strength mainly changes the relative intensities of existing quasiparticle-interference features. In a self-consistent two-vortex state, the Josephson response develops a spatially varying phase relative to the condensate. The response and condensate share the winding close to each core, while larger loops enclose additional winding of the Josephson response. The local Josephson sign and phase reflect the anomalous spectrum and the tip--sample coupling.
summary: This theoretical work examines how local Josephson coupling behaves in a two-orbital $s_{\pm}$ superconductor near impurities and vortices. The authors find that impurities can significantly alter the local coupling sign by redistributing spectral weight, and the Josephson phase exhibits complex spatial variations around vortex cores. This work provides detailed signatures for probing superconducting symmetry using scanning tunneling microscopy techniques.
main_problem: The study investigates the local Josephson response in a two-orbital $s_{\pm}$ superconductor when subjected to nonmagnetic impurities or when near superconducting vortices.
main_result: Nonmagnetic impurities can redistribute anomalous spectral contributions to reverse the local Josephson coupling sign without requiring a $\pi$ phase shift in the bond pair fields. Furthermore, the Josephson response develops a spatially varying phase in the presence of multiple vortices.
method: The analysis employs theoretical calculations using the Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) Hamiltonian, calculating the local Josephson coefficient ($K_i$) via integrals over the imaginary frequency axis.
model_or_system: The system is a two-orbital $s_{\pm}$ superconductor, modeled using two Fe sublattices with $d_{xz}$ and $d_{yz}$ orbitals, motivated by iron arsenide compounds. The calculations are performed self-consistently on a lattice structure.
key_observables: Local Josephson response (sign and phase), local bond pair field magnitude ($|\psi_i|$), and the local anomalous Green function ($F_{i\alpha}(z)$).
important_parameters: Impurity potential strength ($V_{	ext{imp}}$), tip gap ($\Delta_t$), and the superconducting gap structure ($s_{\pm}$ pairing).
main_assumptions: The tip is modeled as an ideal $s$-wave reservoir, and Zeeman and spin–orbit couplings are omitted from the primary analysis.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the model structure, the spatial profiles of the bond magnitude ($A_i$), pair field magnitude ($|\psi_i|$), and Josephson coupling magnitude ($|K_i|$) near impurities and vortices, showing distinct spatial variations.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the model and the measurement technique (JSTM). It then analyzes the effect of impurities on the local Josephson coupling, followed by a detailed examination of the spatial phase variation of the response in a two-vortex state.
why_interesting: The detailed mapping of local superconducting order parameters and their response to disorder (impurities) and topological defects (vortices) provides insights into the robustness and symmetry of unconventional superconductivity, which is relevant to understanding exotic quantum states.

Panels (b,d): individual cumulative coefficients for Ec ≥2, retaining all contributions below 2. Panels (a,b) refer to the center (31, 15); panels (c,d) refer to the off-center site (29, 13). Ec is a BdG eigenenergy cutoff, not a bias voltage or an imaginary-frequency cutoff.

FIG. 4. Tip-gap dependence of the signed Josephson coefficient at (a) the impurity center (31, 15) and (b) the off-center site (29, 13). The sample states and global phase convention are unchanged throughout the scan. Lines connect the calculated coefficients at the sampled tip gaps; the zero crossings are not fitted.

Panels (a,c) refer to the impurity center (31, 15) and panels (b,d) to the off-center site (29, 13). Upper row: CPRs for Vimp = 0.05.
